subject: Recap & next steps — throughput/latency needs for NobleHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@noblehealth.com>, Tim Boyd <tim.boyd@noblehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps — throughput/latency needs for NobleHealth

Hi Alice / Tim — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call so we have alignment and clear next steps.

TL;DR
- Primary goal: replace an on-prem ensemble with a hosted/dedicated inference stack for patient-facing summarization and clinician note generation.
- Key pain: current infra can’t meet latency spikes during daytime load leading to dropped requests and manual fallbacks.
- Target SLOs discussed: p50 <= 220ms, p95 <= 650ms for responses up to ~256 tokens; steady-state throughput ~40 RPS with allowed bursts to ~120 RPS.

What we heard (pain & impact)
- Latency sensitivity: clinician workflow requires sub-second completions for short summaries (250–300 tokens). Delays >1s force manual review and slow throughput.
- Variable traffic: predictable daily peaks 09:00–16:00 ET, roughly 3x baseline traffic; occasional batch processing overnight.
- Compliance: data residency must remain in US regions; SOC2 evidence required for procurement.

Model & quality constraints
- You prefer an instruction-tuned open model (strong on summarization and PII redaction). On the call you mentioned evaluating 13B-class variants; we discussed rdw-13b-instruct as a candidate.
- Need to preserve hallucination controls and deterministic reranking for sensitive outputs.

Initial technical recommendations (high-level)
- Start with a Dedicated pool in US-East with reserved capacity to meet steady-state SLOs and burst capacity for daytime spikes.
- Use 4-bit quantization for cost efficiency while validating no quality regressions on your prompt set.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated patient-context queries to reduce per-token compute.

Agreed next steps
1) Rishi (cc’d) will provide a short technical deep-dive with topology options and estimated perf numbers (by EOD tomorrow).
2) Marissa (me) will share the SOC2 + security questionnaire you requested (attached).
3) NobleHealth to share a small prompt set (10–20 representative prompts) and a sample traffic profile so we can run a bench.
4) Procurement timeline: Tim mentioned a target decision by end of next month — please confirm.

Attachments: NobleHealth_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (security/compliance answers you requested).

If I missed anything or the numbers above need to be tightened, flag it and I’ll update. Thanks again — we’ll follow up with the technical write-up from Rishi.

— Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-13T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Technical deep-dive: topology & perf estimates (initial)

Hi Alice / team — following Marissa’s recap, here’s an initial technical proposal and the perf estimates based on the workload characteristics you described. This is meant to be conservative and to surface tradeoffs.

Assumptions
- Target response size: 150–300 tokens (avg 230 tokens)
- Concurrent steady-state load: 40 RPS; daytime bursts to 120 RPS for ~2 hours
- Model candidate: rdw-13b-instruct (we’ll A/B with a quantized 13B + a trimmed 7B variant for cost/fallbacks)
- Hardware preference: US-East, NVIDIA A100/80GB (we can size for H100 if preferred)

Recommended topology (Dedicated Reserved Pool)
- Primary pool: 4 x A100 (80GB) nodes running rdw-13b-instruct quantized to 4-bit (nf4) with per-node concurrency tuned.
- Warm pool: 2 x A100 nodes kept at low-power to enable burst scaling (hot-attach) and avoid cold-start latencies.
- Autoscaler policy: target CPU/GPU utilization 65% -> scale out by 1 node; aggressive burst policy allows +3 nodes for 10–20 min windows.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated patient context and a per-route short-term LRU cache for identical prompt hashes.
- Routing: primary to Dedicated pool (low-latency), fallback to a lower-cost 7B-compatible variant for degraded availability.

Perf estimates (lab -> expected production with warm cache)
- 256-token generation (rdw-13b-instruct, 4-bit)
  - p50: ~180 ms
  - p95: ~540 ms
  - sustained throughput: ~45 RPS across primary pool (4 nodes)
  - burst capability (with warm pool): 120–140 RPS for short windows (2–15 minutes)

Notes on tradeoffs
- Quantization (4-bit) reduces GPU memory footprint and cost but requires a quick quality verification pass on your prompt set — we’ll run a focused eval.
- Batching increases throughput but can add tail latency; for clinician-facing paths we recommend keeping batch windows small (max batch delay 20–30ms) and prefer dynamic continuous batching.
- KV/prefix caching will significantly reduce cost and latency for repeated patient-context calls, but we need examples to estimate hit rates.

Pilot offer
- We can run a 2-week pilot on Dedicated in US-East with telemetry (token-level cost, p50/p95 by route) and a lightweight SLA for the pilot window. If that looks good we’ll convert to a reserved commit.

Attachments: proposed_architecture_diagram.png, perf_estimates_table.csv (rough numbers above in CSV form).

Questions for you
1) Can you confirm the hit-rate expectation for repeated patient context (e.g., % of requests with identical prefix)?
2) Any hard limit on batch delay for clinician UX (we used 20–30ms as a guideline)?

Happy to hop on a short follow-up to walk through the diagram.

— Rishi
